authoredFrom: SQLD5 (M60 SQL wave, 2026-09-26). Quoting measured by bb_tests/sql/probe/grammar-gaps.mts (cases quoted-ident / backtick-ident / bracket-ident) and column-name loss by probe/field-introspection.mts: the grammar's name field for a QUOTED identifier is a `literal`, not an `identifier`, and the column reader's identifierTypes set did not include it — so `("Id" int)` produced no column symbol at all, silently. CTE scoping measured by the same probe (case cte-outer-real-table): `WITH x AS (…) SELECT * FROM x JOIN public.x` emitted zero relationships. The nested-CTE-body scoping defect was measured by `script/m12/verify-analyzer.ts sql` against the same 84 facts: 1 false positive, `FP rel:Queries.sql:uses:global:recent_users`, precision 0.988. Giving the sweep the CTE scope of the statement it descends into takes it to precision 1.000 / 0 FP.
comment: The quoted COLUMN is the load-bearing row: it is the symbol that was silently absent, and an expect-only fixture for the table would have passed while it was missing.

expectRelationships.note: `s.d5_real` from the JOIN. It shares the SHAPE of the phantom with nothing: a qualified reference whose leaf is a declared real table. Publishing it is the positive half of the pair - the fix must suppress the CTE body reference without suppressing this.

forbidRelationships.note: The nested-CTE-body shape. `d5_first` IS a CTE, so no table by that name exists and no `uses` edge to it may exist from anywhere in this file - including from inside `d5_second`'s own body, which the declaration sweep dispatches as a separate `statement`. Before the scope fix the sweep published `uses global->d5_first` from that body while the outer SELECT's `d5_second` was suppressed correctly by the same guard.

note: `uses global->d5_cte` is present BECAUSE of `s.d5_cte` — the bare `d5_cte` is the CTE and is suppressed, the qualified one is a real table. Both have leaf `d5_cte`, so the edge existing at all is the assertion: before the fix the file emitted no relationship whatsoever.
